Hi Caroline / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and appreciate the context on Acme's prioritized use cases (customer support triage + automated policy decisions). Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) What we heard:
- Primary goal: reduce average response time and surface confident, low-hallucination suggestions for CS agents.
- Hard requirement: <1% critical hallucination rate on policy-related prompts; audit logs retained 12 months.
- Throughput target: ~200 req/s with peak bursts to 400 req/s.

2) Redwood differentiation we discussed:
- Unified runtime with built-in KV/prefix caching to reduce cost without impacting latency.
- Verified performance profiles for open models + fallbacks to smaller variants to preserve SLOs.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdowns and per-route error/hallucination monitoring.

3) Next tests we propose (quick wins):
- Run our model-quality eval suite you shared against the same prompt set across: Redwood-hosted model (opt-7b-quant), Bedrock/Anthropic baseline, and OpenAI GPT-x baseline.
- Regression checks: exact-match, F1 for QA prompts, and hallucination detection rate (manual sampling + automated classifier).
- Deliverable: short report with confusion cases and recommended model/config (quantization/batching) by EOD Tue (next week).

4) Action items:
- I've attached a quick matrix (redwood-vs-hyperscalers-quick-matrix.pdf) summarizing the differences we discussed.
- Can you send the canonical prompt set you want us to use? If you prefer, we can start with the sample prompts you ran in the deck.
- I'll loop in Aditya (solutions) and Marcus (ML eng) to coordinate the hands-on tests and schedule a runbook session.

If that aligns, I'll schedule a 60-min runbook session for next Wed where we can execute the first pass live.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa / Caroline — quick technical note and proposed thresholds from our side: 

Baseline notes (from prior customer evals on similar CS/policy prompts):
- OpenAI baseline (gpt-4o-like): observed critical-hallucination ~1.8% on policy prompts (manual sample), calibration slightly overconfident in low-context cases.
- Bedrock-managed model (PaLM-family): ~2.3% critical-hallucination on our sampled policy set.
- Redwood-hosted opt-7b-quant (default config): ~1.2% critical-hallucination after prefix caching + 2-shot prompts; P95 latency ~280ms in single-tenant tests.

Suggested regression checks / pass criteria:
- Critical hallucination rate <= 1.0% (manual sample of 200) for policy prompts to pass initial security bar.
- Confidence calibration: expected probability bands should align within +/- 10% of observed correctness per bucket.
- Latency: P95 <= 350ms for single-request; under 200 req/s sustained, P95 <= 450ms.

Proposed test assets (we'll provide):
- eval_runner.sh (sample script to run the prompt set across endpoints)
- hallucination_classifier.pkl (for automated pre-filtering before manual audit)
- sample auditing spreadsheet with redaction-friendly fields

I'll schedule the runbook session for next Wed 11:00 AM PT — sending invite now. During the session we'll: ingest prompts, walk through the eval runner, and kick off the first batch.

On logs retention: Redwood-hosted audit logs can be retained up to 13 months (enterprise plan). We can export logs in JSONL with timestamps and matched-request ids for your compliance team.
